evidence: Local re-implementation of boolean recognition instead of reusing `inferInput` against a doc note to mark superseded.

panel.summary: Case-insensitive TRUE/FALSE recognition is re-implemented locally instead of reusing the existing shared boolean recognition in `inferInput` (`input.ts:241-247`), which the issue itself cites as the precedent. A tiny shared helper (e.g. `isBooleanLiteral`/`parseBooleanLiteral`) exported from `input.ts` would keep the two case-folding rules in lockstep; the inline version can drift if input parsing ever accepts more boolean spellings. The no-allocation argument is real but could live inside such a helper. Preference, not a blocker.
panel.evidence: data-validation.ts:163-167 does `value.toUpperCase() === CHECKBOX_TRUE` while input.ts:241-247 already lower-cases and compares to 'true'/'false'.
